discovery: Spherical-aberration correction in electron optics, enabling sub-ångström transmission electron microscopy
subfield: Electron optics / materials physics (transmission electron microscopy)
motivation: For half a century Scherzer's theorem held that round electron lenses have unavoidable spherical aberration, limiting resolution far above the electron wavelength. Rose designed the hexapole corrector; Haider built it; Urban demonstrated in 1998 with them that aberration-corrected TEM works, achieving atomic resolution free of delocalisation artefacts. This solved a fundamental problem in charged-particle optics and transformed physics of condensed matter: individual atomic columns, light elements, interfaces, dopants and defects can now be imaged and quantified directly, with chemical sensitivity via EELS and EDS. In my own field, aberration-corrected (S)TEM revealed the atomic structure of the nanoscale precipitates that strengthen aluminium alloys, guiding industrial alloy design. Today corrected instruments are standard in laboratories worldwide, underpinning research in semiconductors, catalysis, batteries, quantum materials and biology. This is instrumentation that let us see what was invisible.
